characters.pronunciationInstruction: The display/system name is ARI, but ALL spoken dialogue must say อาริ. Never send the letters A-R-I to TTS as spoken text. Pronounce อาริ as Ah-ree, two syllables.

continuityRules.names: System/display names remain C-SHARP and ARI only in metadata. Spoken Thai uses ซีชาร์ป and อาริ. Never place the literal strings C-SHARP or ARI inside image prompts as visible character labels.
continuityRules.promptRoleNames: Inside imageDescription and videoPrompt, refer to them as older brother and younger brother rather than literal character names. This reduces accidental nameplates and text rendering.
continuityRules.noNameplates: STRICT: no character names, usernames, floating labels, overhead tags, chat bubbles, health bars, score text, subtitles, captions, badges with letters, or readable UI anywhere near the characters. Prefer no readable text anywhere in frame unless the story absolutely requires a prop sign.
continuityRules.dialogue: Use one speaking character per scene. The non-speaking brother must keep his mouth closed and react naturally. Keep each line short enough for one 8-second scene.
continuityRules.visualIdentity: Both brothers are stylized East Asian boys with fair/light skin and dark-brown hair. The older brother is consistently taller with a rounded-square face; the younger brother is consistently shorter with a rounder face and slightly larger eyes. Keep the exact same face geometry, outfit, skin tone, hair silhouette, props and body proportions across all 10 EP.
continuityRules.previousSceneReference: For scene 2 onward, when location/time/action continues, use the immediately previous generated scene image as the primary visual continuity reference. Preserve the exact face design, skin tone, hair silhouette, outfit, props, relative height, screen direction, obstacle state and lighting. Character identity must not reset between scenes.
continuityRules.dialoguePronunciation: ARI is metadata only. Spoken name must always be อาริ (Ah-ree), two syllables. Never put ARI as spoken text. Spoken C-SHARP should be ซีชาร์ป in Thai dialogue.
